A group of crows is called a murder.

The text provided contains a classic social engineering tactic known as a Business Email Compromise (BEC) or spear-phishing attack. The attacker exploits urgency ("immediate action required") and authority (impersonating the CEO) to pressure employees into bypassing security protocols. By instructing staff to send sensitive customer data to an external email under the guise of "safekeeping," the attacker aims to steal proprietary information or customer data. This relies on manipulating human psychology—specifically fear of data loss and deference to authority—rather than technical hacking methods.
